title: A complete diploid human genome benchmark for personalized genomics.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed the marbl/hg002 GitHub repo (3 markdown files only) and read its README (CC0 licence, release links). HEAD on hg002v1.2.fasta.gz: 1,769,811,265 bytes, over the 50 MB cap, not downloaded. Downloaded three assembly patch VCFs (version-to-version corrections) from marbl/HG002-issues: v0.9->v1.0 has 6,568 records, v1.0.1->v1.1 has 4,013, v1.1->v1.2 has 5,651. These are lists of edited positions (FILTER=AUTO, alignment-derived INFO fields), not a feature/label table.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 99.4% near-perfect coverage, 19,956 maternal / 19,190 paternal protein-coding genes, 2-7% more sequence resolved by de novo assembly, and the claim that the v1.2 release patched 612 problematic regions (README). Supplement not retrievable (Europe PMC supplementaryFiles timed out).

a1_downloadable.note: Public CC0 S3 and GitHub downloads, no login needed. The main FASTA (1.77 GB) is over the 50 MB cap, so only metadata was recorded for it.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked in files. The resource is a reference genome sequence (an assembly). No outcome column exists. The closest thing to a label, 'assembly error here', would have to be built by turning patch VCF edits into positives and choosing every other position as a negative.

a3_inputs_present.note: Sequence is present in the FASTA, but extracting context windows needs the 1.77 GB file.

a4_units_stated.note: Not applicable: genomic coordinates and bases only.

a5_enough_rows.note: Sum of the records in the three patch VCFs I counted (6,568 + 4,013 + 5,651). Not deduplicated, and versions use different coordinate systems.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~1.8 GB compressed FASTA plus <5 MB of VCFs
a6_fits_laptop.note: Feasible after streaming the windows out of the FASTA.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: README says v1.2 patched 612 problematic regions, but the v1.1->v1.2 VCF has 5,651 records. These could be regions versus individual edits, but I couldn't confirm that.

a8_label_provenance.note: Corrections came largely from automated polishing pipelines: variant callers such as DeepVariant run on aligned reads (FILTER=AUTO, AQ quality fields), plus manual curation. An 'error' label would partly distil those callers' outputs.

existing_models.name: DeepPolisher (Google, encoder-only transformer for assembly polishing; Genome Research 2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: Trained on HG002 Q100 v0.9 truth, chromosomes 1-19, held-out chromosomes. Cut assembly errors 43% (8.14 to 4.72 per Mb).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved beyond the search summary.

backbone.name: Nucleotide Transformer / DNABERT-2 (DNA language models) would be the only fit

integration.partner_dataset: GIAB (Genome in a Bottle) HG002 variant benchmarks
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Which sequence contexts stay hard to assemble even with the best long reads? That is already the subject of tools like DeepPolisher.

controls.positive_control: Homopolymer runs and tandem repeats should be enriched for corrections.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle the error labels across positions.
controls.external_validation: Patches from a later assembly release (temporal split by version).

honest_claim_h3: At best: it would predict where automated polishers plus curators chose to edit one individual's assembly, not where assembly errors really are.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the DNA sequence around a position to predict whether the best human genome assembly needed a correction there.
plain_idea.train_on: Short DNA windows from one person's (HG002) complete genome. About 16,232 edited positions across three releases, plus sampled unedited positions as negatives.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a position was corrected between assembly releases, taken from the project's patch files (VCF lists of edits) that polishing software and curators produced.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Genome assemblers would learn which DNA contexts are still error-prone. But read-based polishers already target this better.

more_or_better_data.why: DeepPolisher already trains directly on this HG002 Q100 truth assembly and uses read alignments, which carry more information than sequence alone.

confidence_score.why: There's one individual and no replicate assemblies, so per-prediction noise can't be estimated.

models_beatable.why: DeepPolisher (2024-2025 transformer) is evaluated on held-out chromosomes and uses read evidence we wouldn't have.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No new data measures the same quantity the same way. A sequence-only model would see less than the baseline, not more.

ml_idea: Classify the sequence context of assembly-correction sites from the HG002 patch VCFs against sampled unedited positions. The labels are constructed and partly come from polishing software.

effort.compute_note: Estimated only. Nothing was timed, and the FASTA was not downloaded.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Lift all patch VCFs onto one coordinate system and count unique non-telomere edits. Done, it still lacks a label column (A2).

verdict_reason: This is a reference genome assembly, not a labelled table (A2). The only usable label, assembly-correction sites, would have to be built from patch VCFs that polishing software partly produced (A8). DeepPolisher already trains on this same truth set.
